cited_evidence.text: Ni-based superalloys have been extensively employed as critical high-temperature structural materials used in aerospace engineering and the power generation industry due to their superior high-temperature mechanical properties, which are derived from the combination of 60–70% volume fraction of ordered γ′ precipitates (L12) coherently embedded in the solid-solution γ matrix (FCC-A1) []. The alloy design of Ni-based superalloys has approached its limit for performance enhancements due to the constraints of Ni-based systems. A novel concept in alloy design, high entropy alloys (HEAs), has made a breakthrough in conventional alloys by revisiting the vast composition space []. Precipitation-strengthened HEAs, as newly emerging structural materials, are highly attractive due to their combination of strength and ductility [,,,,,,]. Compared to grain boundary strengthening and solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening of multicomponent L12 nanoprecipitates can significantly improve the yield strength of HEAs while maintaining good ductility. decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the mechanical properties of magnetic-refrigeration materials while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect. Earlier studies have explored the use of high-entropy alloys, microstructural optimization, and thermal or thermomechanical treatments to achieve this goal. Recent studies have shown that the introduction of coherent ordered nanoprecipitates, tuning of crystallographic structures, and optimization of processing routes can lead to significant improvements in mechanical performance without compromising the magnetocaloric effect.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made, the development of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials with improved mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect remains a challenge. The optimal combination of composition, microstructure, and processing route to achieve this goal has not been fully established.
decision.why: The introduction of coherent ordered nanoprecipitates has been shown to significantly improve the mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys while retaining their soft magnetic properties. This approach could be applied to MnNiSi-based materials to enhance their mechanical performance without compromising their magnetocaloric effect.
